The Ifo Institute reported that the German government utilized a special exemption from the debt brake for defense and security spending to create additional fiscal capacity
🛡
This mechanism provided the government with an extra credit limit of 28.6 billion euros in 2025; however, actual increases in defense and security expenditures amounted to only 17.6 billion euros. The Ifo Institute characterized the resulting discrepancy of approximately 11 billion euros as budget space reallocated for other purposes, noting that the volume of new borrowing significantly exceeded the growth in actual defense spending.
⚠️
The Institute expressed concern that the current system permits excessive flexibility in fund reallocation within the budget. In response, the Federal Ministry of Finance rejected these conclusions, describing the study as legally and methodologically flawed. The Ministry clarified that the law does not mandate that every additional euro of debt be directed exclusively to defense, and argued that comparing overall defense spending growth with total new borrowing is inaccurate.
